questions.q: What question is Instance Health built to answer, in contrast to the Slow Request Log from Chapter 1?
options: Whether the instance as a whole is trending slower or more error-prone over time, rather than diagnosing one specific transaction
Exactly which line of script caused one page to load slowly
The exact database query plan for a single transaction
Which user most recently edited a given form
questions.explain: Instance Health aggregates across the whole instance and tracks it over time — it answers a trend question, not a single-transaction question.

questions.q: Which three core metrics does Instance Health track over time?
options: Response times, transaction volume, and error rates
Number of active UI Policies, number of Related Lists, and number of forms
CPU temperature, disk color coding, and network cable length
Number of open incidents only
questions.explain: These three, tracked together over time, reveal whether the instance is genuinely degrading or just busier than usual.

questions.q: Why is a single response-time number, by itself, not very useful in Instance Health?
options: Its value comes from comparison over time — this week against last week, this hour against the same hour yesterday
Response time is never actually measured by ServiceNow
A single number is always proof of a serious problem
Instance Health does not record response time at all
questions.explain: A number only becomes a signal once compared against its own history — that's what the trend view provides.

questions.q: A rising average response time paired with rising transaction volume might mean what, per this lesson?
options: The business is simply busier than usual, not necessarily that the platform itself has degraded
The instance has definitely failed
All scheduled jobs have stopped running
The Slow Request Log has been disabled
questions.explain: Reading the metrics together, rather than in isolation, is what lets you distinguish "busier" from "actually degraded."

questions.q: A user reports one specific incident form was slow just now. Why would opening Instance Health first be the wrong move?
options: Instance Health tracks instance-wide trends, not details about any single transaction, so it has nothing to say about that one event
Instance Health is only accessible to developers, never admins
Instance Health only works on sub-production instances
Instance Health and the Slow Request Log always show identical data
questions.explain: For a single-transaction complaint, the Slow Request Log is the right tool; Instance Health is built for a different, trend-level question.
